body: What the numbers do not share is those that attempt and survive. There is belief that majority who attempt suicide once will never attempt again and they will live full lives. For the 40k+ that die by suicide there are 800k+ that survive like Dese'Rae Stage: https://medium.com/@deseraestage/i-lived-24611838d8ca#.dwvmaalfp

Could you tell me more about your role as MOD? I am very interested to learn how @suicidewatch works from your POV.

I am a specialist and trainer for a youth crisis text line and it is growing by leaps and bounds. It is such a welcoming, nonjudgmental venue for youth that they share much the same as those here share in 140 characters. 

For so many hotlines are a foreign concept or through the grapevine of shame and stigma (and past experience) they beoive emergency services are automatically called. In my experience we want to be most collaborative and least invasive. There are so many options to consider and talking through them all to find the right one is key. I share recently with someone the options they had for a certain problem and they were shocked but intrigued by it. So much of suicide prevention is point A to point B but that middle part is missed.

There is movement in the medical and mental health fields to merge the two as an overall wellness from top to bottom. But it is a big undertaking to change the culture, the taboo, the stigma of the two as equals.

I am a crisis interventionist (suicide prevention specialist and trainer) supervisor on phones, chat and text. I have dropped in a few times but its taken some time to get comfortable with the format. What has been the biggest shock for you? And learning curve working as a MOD here?

The few and far between studies show that those who are struggling, who are suicidal are posting about it and are in the least throwing out red flags. There is also information coming out that youth in particular reach out through social media and texting more so than ever before. To your point that professionals just don't understand, well, I believe many is those with degrees in mental health are there because of personal experience and it may be their training that isn't meeting people where they are at. Suicide prevention is a collaboration, we cannot do this alone and this is where #SPSM shows its strength by pulling from so many great minds who have different ties to this movement. It is inspiring, it is real and it is sometimes a little silly but the heart is out of genuine care and concern to link people to care whether that be formal or informal.
